clue.text: One trimming paper always holds cutter at the end

parts.note: The Times is the newspaper

indicators.note: the word for always holds another letter inside it

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: only the final letter of cutter is taken

explanation.surface: A man cutting up a newspaper keeps a blade at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One trimming' is the definition: to trim is to change sides to suit the times.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimmer adjusts opinions to the prevailing mood, which is exactly what an opportunist does.

clue.text: Charm two Israelis perhaps in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: Israelis exemplify Jews, so two of them give a doubled word

explanation.surface: A pair of Israelis speak of a lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Juju is a West African amulet or fetish, so a charm or magic object.

clue.text: Flies perhaps quizzers have their fingers on

definitions.meaning: insects that buzz, as flies do
quiz contestants keep fingers on the buttons that sound when pressed

explanation.definitionFit: Both flies and the quiz-show buttons make a buzzing noise, so both are things that buzz.

clue.text: Before second drink, how to get oneself off the floor?

definitions.text: how to get oneself off the floor?

parts.note: pre- means before
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders how to stand up again before a second round.
explanation.definitionFit: The gym exercise pushes the body up from the floor with the arms, a humorous description.

clue.text: Advanced forward and hurt, though not at the front

parts.note: a prop is a forward in a rugby scrum

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for hurt is dropped

parts.note: wounded means hurt

explanation.surface: A soldier pushed ahead and was injured, if not on the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like part of the definition with 'Advanced'; it is the rugby PROP.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound is to put forward an idea, so advanced in the sense of proposed.

clue.text: Fear a partnership

parts.note: we denotes two or more people together

explanation.surface: Someone is afraid of entering a partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is reverential fear or dread.

clue.text: A way with money at last, but a lack of interest

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: only the final letter of money is used

explanation.surface: A road to wealth is finally reached, yet nobody cares.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is indifference, the absence of any concern or enthusiasm.

clue.text: People gawping around king like famous emperor newly clothed?

indicators.note: the gawpers stand around the king letter

parts.note: starers are people gawping
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Onlookers crowd round a monarch in his supposed new outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: STARKERS is British slang for stark naked, as the emperor in the fairy tale was in his 'new clothes'.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor in the tale wore nothing at all, which is the slang meaning stark naked.

clue.text: Do wobbly moves, on receiving this?

definitions.text: Do wobbly moves, on receiving this?

indicators.note: the letters move around to new positions

explanation.surface: A punched boxer staggers about after taking a heavy hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: you wobble after receiving one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard punch to the torso makes a fighter reel, a heavy setback.

clue.text: Back slogan opposing Queen's English? It's a little bit charged

indicators.note: back says the slogan is read from end to start

parts.note: a protest slogan against RP, received pronunciation, would be no to RP

explanation.surface: A protest chant against posh accents is rather heated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like support (PRO), but it reverses the slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle carries a positive electric charge, so a tiny charged bit.

clue.text: Way to lose a stick

indicators.note: to lose says the named letter goes

parts.note: a road is a way

explanation.surface: Someone loses their walking stick on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a slender stick or pole.

clue.text: For traveller, staff replace stolen pack

indicators.note: to replace the letters is to put them back in a new order

explanation.surface: A hiker asks for a staff to replace a stolen rucksack.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpine walking staff with an iron spike, carried by mountain travellers.

clue.text: To reduce work is good — admitted by a woman blushing?

indicators.note: the woman lets the letter for good inside her

parts.note: a bride is traditionally described as blushing

explanation.surface: Cutting down on work is welcome news to a shy young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a book is to shorten it.

clue.text: Medicinal plant extremely useless? Not unknown

indicators.note: not says the unknown letter is left out

parts.note: very vain means extremely useless, vain being futile
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy is utterly ineffective, though that is not certain.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena officinalis, a herb long used in folk remedies.

clue.text: Has a portion of meat, say

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone helps themselves to a serving of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a meal is to consume food, as in having dinner.

clue.text: Carriage with everybody arriving at city boundary

parts.note: a berlin is a four-wheeled covered carriage
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A coach full of people reaches the edge of town.
explanation.definitionFit: The barrier divided East and West in the German capital from 1961 to 1989.

clue.text: Train needs energy except for reversing

indicators.note: reversing turns the pair of pieces end to end

parts.note: but means except for

explanation.surface: A locomotive requires power, other than when going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: A TUBE train runs on the London Underground, which is nicknamed the Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Underground railway is called the Tube, and its trains are tube trains.

clue.text: In dark, street guide leads to a dance

indicators.note: the guide sits inside the word for dark

parts.note: murk is darkness
the A-Z is a British street atlas

explanation.surface: In the gloom, a street map leads someone to a dance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-Z is a well-known British book of city street maps.
explanation.definitionFit: A Polish folk dance in triple time.

clue.text: Pick everything up to clean table

definitions.meaning: win every prize or trick on offer
literally brush everything off a table top

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to win all the prizes, and literally to clear the table top.

clue.text: Save two pieces of snooker equipment, one too short

indicators.note: one of the two items loses its final letter

parts.note: a rest supports the cue in snooker
a cue is the stick used to strike the ball

explanation.surface: A snooker player saves two bits of kit, one of which is too short.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue is to save from danger.

clue.text: Quickly deal with operating system change in midweek

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the middle of week
mid picks the central letters of week

parts.note: XP was a Windows operating system
to edit is to change

explanation.surface: An IT department rushes through a software update midweek.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite a task is to speed it up or dispatch it promptly.

clue.text: Away from the Capitol in cheerful mood

parts.note: up means in good spirits
a state is a mood, as in a state of mind

explanation.surface: A politician is in good spirits after leaving Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: The Capitol suggests Washington, but in US usage upstate means away from a state's main city.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage, upstate means the rural part of a state far from its big city.

clue.text: Nasty, as a sun and planet explode

indicators.note: exploding blows the letters apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A star and planet blow up, which sounds horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasant means disagreeable, which is what nasty means.

clue.text: Family of trees maybe that help to protect our coastline

definitions.text: that help to protect our coastline

parts.note: elder is a kind of tree
brethren are members of a family or fellowship

explanation.surface: A family tree belongs to a group guarding Britain's coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elder Brethren run Trinity House, which maintains lighthouses around England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior members of Trinity House oversee the lighthouses and buoys around the coast.

clue.text: Gibraltar native to chatter foolishly in pub, 16

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: in puts the chatter inside the run of pub and bare

parts.note: 16 across means naked, so bare
to yap is to talk foolishly

explanation.surface: A Gibraltarian prattles nonsense in a pub with no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: The tailless macaques living on the Rock are the only wild monkeys in Europe.

clue.text: Take part, adding in line for total

indicators.note: the line letter is added inside

parts.note: to compete is to take part

explanation.surface: A form-filler takes part by adding a line to reach the total.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete means entire or total, as in a complete failure.

clue.text: Encyclopaedist cheated with the majority of titillating material

parts.note: did, as in did someone out of money, means cheated

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letters dropped

parts.note: erotica is sexually titillating material

explanation.surface: A reference-book writer cheated by including racy material.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot edited the great French Encyclopédie of the Enlightenment.

clue.text: Two cats circle wildly, a touching display

indicators.note: wildly says the letters are scrambled
two says the word is used twice

parts.note: taken as cat, singular
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: Two cats circle each other in an affectionate show.
explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from Italian toccare, to touch: a keyboard display piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso keyboard piece showing off the player's touch.

clue.text: Tolstoy's hero's about to speak tearfully

indicators.note: about turns the name round end to end

parts.note: Levin is the hero of Anna Karenina

explanation.surface: A Russian novel's hero is about to talk through tears.
explanation.definitionFit: To snivel is to whine or cry snuffling.

clue.text: Actress at first put on nothing in indigo

indicators.note: only the opening letter of actress is taken

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: An actress initially wears nothing but blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo shrub and the blue dye obtained from it.
